standard_prerequisites.name: Pure ideals and the generation of a finitely generated pure ideal by an idempotent
standard_prerequisites.use: Is the step that converts absolute flatness into idempotent generation of principal ideals.

standard_prerequisites.name: The connection between idempotents and open-and-closed subsets of the spectrum, and the criterion on rings with only minimal primes being a field
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives that every prime is maximal and, with nilpotence, that A is reduced.

standard_prerequisites.name: A ring all of whose local rings are fields has all modules flat
standard_prerequisites.use: Closes the cycle by giving (4) implies (2).

core_obligations: Record that (1) and (2) are equivalent immediately (proof line 30261).
Assume A is absolutely flat and conclude that every ideal is pure, hence that every finitely generated ideal is generated by an idempotent (proof lines 30265-30268).
For f in A use (f) = (e) with e idempotent, so that D(f) = D(e) is open and closed, and conclude that every prime ideal of A is maximal (proof lines 30269-30273).
Conclude that A is reduced: if f is nilpotent then e = 0 and hence f = 0 (proof lines 30274-30275).
Show (3) implies (4): if A is reduced and every prime is maximal, then every local ring of A is a field (proof lines 30278-30280).
Show (4) implies (2): if every local ring of A is a field then every A-module is flat, so A is absolutely flat (proof lines 30283-30285).
difficulty_reason: The lemma establishes the equivalence of four conditions on a ring A: that A have weak dimension at most 0; that A be absolutely flat; that A be reduced with every prime maximal; and that every local ring of A be a field (source lines 30249-30258). The equivalence of (1) and (2) is immediate. The substantive part is (1) implies (3): assuming A absolutely flat, every ideal of A is pure, so every finitely generated ideal is generated by an idempotent by the finitely-generated-pure-ideal lemma; for f in A one then has (f) = (e) for an idempotent e, so D(f) = D(e) is open and closed, which makes every prime ideal maximal by the criterion on rings with only minimal primes, and if f is nilpotent then e = 0 and hence f = 0, so A is reduced (proof lines 30264-30275). The implication (3) implies (4) is immediate from the description of local rings of a reduced ring whose primes are all maximal, and (4) implies (2) because if every local ring is a field then every module is flat (proof lines 30278-30285). The non-routine content is the passage from purity of ideals to idempotent generation and the resulting open-and-closed structure of the spectrum.
